full.description: This is a high-power photomicrograph of a skin or mucosal biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The section shows stratified squamous epithelium at the top with an underlying dense, diffuse inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of plasma cells and lymphocytes. Numerous small blood vessels are visible within the inflammatory stroma. These histologic features are characteristic of a primary syphilitic chancre.

random.description: This is a high-power photomicrograph of tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The image displays a stratified squamous epithelium overlying a dense, chronic inflammatory infiltrate composed predominantly of lymphocytes and plasma cells. The histological appearance is consistent with chronic inflammation, such as chronic cervicitis or chronic urethritis. The dense leukocytic infiltration beneath the mucosal surface is the primary pathological finding.
